To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The use of qualitative research interviews is increasing in the health sciences; (2) Qualitative interviews are used in a wide variety of research settings, including both clinical and nonclinical settings, with both healthy and ill subjects; (3) Qualitative interviews have been used to study a broad range of topics in the health sciences, including patient-provider interactions, the process and outcome of medical decision making, the process of medical care, and the process and outcome in the delivery of health care

the nature and consequences of the social construction of the world in which we live, and with the nature of the social processes through which this construction occurs.
the social and psychological processes that underlie the creation and maintenance of social networks.
